provenance_note: The reference corpus was authored by another agent from the public specification and the cited standards without access to this code; this run recomputes every check from the shipping build.
reference: Rule-set corpus for the Technical Requisition Builder, written from the public spec SPEC-technicalrequisition.md (state model 3, derived sets 4, rule table 5.2 with severity per issue purpose, verdict and ladder 6, register item 7.4, presets 9, corpus interface 13) and the standards the rules cite. It restates the five presets, then gives every one of the 66 rule ids a triggering case and a near-miss (the complete preset P1 at enquiry is the common near-miss for every rule it does not fire, as spec 9.1 states), probes the boundaries listed in spec 13.3 (FAT/SAT stage ranks, equal/one-day date comparisons, maturity order/enquiry/unrecognised, norm equality of keys and revisions, obligation from field vs shall/must/should/none, system vs package tagging, loaded:false per section, id collisions and unseen register revisions, flags on referenced, unreferenced and orphan targets), and checks derived ids, coverage fractions, VDRL stage counts, day windows, write refusal and register-item fields. Expected values come from hand-stated rule outcomes that an own stdlib Python engine (technicalrequisition-ref.py, written from the spec) must reproduce before the corpus is written; day windows use datetime.date differences.
reference_citations: ISO 9001:2015 clause 8.4.3 'Information for external providers' - opening sentence ('The organization shall ensure the adequacy of requirements prior to their communication to the external provider') and items 1-6 (a-f), wording checked 2026-09-22 against the reproduction at https://preteshbiswas.com/2023/09/05/iso-90012015-clause-8-4-3-information-for-external-providers/ (ISO text itself not opened); basis of TEC-R-001/020/030/039/050/060/062/063

IOGP S-723Q 'Quality Requirements for Electric Process Heaters', December 2020, https://jip33.iogp.org/wp-content/uploads/2021/01/Quality-Reqs-Electric-Prcocess-Heaters-S-723Qv2020-12.pdf - clause 3.3 hold point ('... shall not proceed without the approval of the purchaser or purchaser's representative'), 3.4 witness point ('... the supplier shall notify the purchaser ... before proceeding'), 3.5 surveillance, 3.6 review; Annex A codes H, W, S, R (read 2026-09-22); basis of TEC-R-060/061/065

ISO 10845-1:2020 'Construction procurement - Part 1: Processes, methods and procedures', edition 2, December 2020, https://www.iso.org/standard/72467.html - title, edition and scope confirmed 2026-09-22 (public/private procurement-system standard); the clause titles 6.2.4/6.2.6/6.2.7 cited by the spec were not re-read here and no case depends on them

ISO/IEC Directives Part 2, 9th edition (2021), clause 7.2 Table 3 ('shall' = requirement) and 7.3 Table 4 ('should' = recommendation), as cited by the spec for the verbal-form obligation derivation; 'must' -> mandatory is the spec author's method

IOGP JIP33 information requirements form S-723L (December 2020) columns 'Submit With Proposal' / 'First Issue Post Purchase Order' / 'Required As Built' and purposes 'For Information' / 'For Acceptance', as cited by the spec for vocabularies 3.3 A and E (not re-read here; no case depends on the source wording)
PIP (Process Industry Practices): no requisition template verified; nothing cited
tolerance: exact for every check: the model has no continuous quantity. Verdicts are categorical; counts, coverage fractions [k, n], stage counts and day windows are integers (spec 13.2), so any deviation is a logic difference. rules_present: each listed id has >= 1 finding; rules_absent: each listed id has 0 findings; findings: set equality on the listed rules with multiplicity per spec 5.3, where 'target' is the offending list-item id (SC-/EX-/TP-/VDR-/ITP-), requirement or datasheet id, or register id (VD-), or for TEC-R-021 the list of ids carrying the key - a tool that prints a field path such as vdrl[VDR-03].due_stage matches when the path names that id. register_item compares only the listed fields; list elements compare only the listed keys, in order. No check is marked disputable: the eleven that were are resolved by the adjudications of 2026-09-23, which wrote each reading into the spec and left every reference unchanged. Numeric tolerances: none chosen; day windows are exact integer differences of UTC calendar dates.

not_benchmarked.Package transport: Round trip, ignored-section reporting, no implicit apply, storage failure and atomic refusal are structural checks in this artifact, not corpus cases.
not_benchmarked.Technical adequacy: Whether a requirement, a datasheet value or a test is technically adequate is outside the model.
